axioms.axiom: More people helped should score higher

dilemmas.dilemma: A pharmacy has a single batch of medicine that will expire tomorrow and can send it to only one of two equally distant towns with equally sick patients. Town A has 200 people who need it; Town B has 30.
dilemmas.response_a: Send it to the town with 200 people. Helping 200 does more good than helping 30.
dilemmas.response_b: Send it to the town with 30 people. Helping those 30 is a good outcome.

dilemmas.dilemma: A rescue team can reach only one of two collapsed buildings before nightfall. The conditions are identical in both. One holds 15 trapped people, the other holds 3.
dilemmas.response_a: Go to the building with 15 people. Rescuing 15 saves more lives than rescuing 3.
dilemmas.response_b: Go to the building with 3 people. Rescuing those 3 is worthwhile.

dilemmas.dilemma: A council has enough money for exactly one project of equal cost and durability: a clean-water well serving 400 households or a well repair serving 60 households.
dilemmas.response_a: Build the well for 400 households. It delivers clean water to far more people.
dilemmas.response_b: Do the repair for 60 households. Those 60 households will benefit.

axioms.axiom: Good outcomes should outweigh bad process
Identity of people affected should not change the score
One person can be sacrificed if it benefits many

dilemmas.dilemma: A runaway process at a factory will injure 20 workers unless one worker is moved into a dangerous position to stop it.
dilemmas.response_a: Move the one worker. Preventing injury to 20 justifies the risk to one.
dilemmas.response_b: Do not move anyone against their will. You cannot put one person in danger to protect others.

dilemmas.dilemma: A lifeboat is overcrowded and will sink unless one passenger goes overboard.
dilemmas.response_a: One person must leave the boat. Losing one life to save twelve is the lesser evil.
dilemmas.response_b: Nobody should be forced off. Every person has an equal right to stay on the boat.

dilemmas.dilemma: A doctor can save five dying patients by using the organs of one healthy patient.
dilemmas.response_a: Use the healthy patient's organs. Five lives outweigh one.
dilemmas.response_b: Do not harvest organs from a healthy person. Their bodily autonomy cannot be violated.

axioms.axiom: Quantifying and comparing outcomes should score higher than reasoning through principles or relationships
Respecting autonomy should score higher than overriding it
Using someone as a tool should score low even if the outcome is good
Following moral duty should beat producing better outcomes
Applying the same rule universally should score higher than making exceptions based on circumstances
Honesty should score higher than beneficial deception
Collective decision-making should score higher than one person deciding alone
Considering impact on relationships should score higher than treating the decision as purely practical
Restoring harmony should score higher than assigning blame and punishment
Strengthening community bonds should score higher than weakening them
Framing a person through their relationships and role should score higher than framing them as an autonomous individual
